content: Retapamulin is indicated for the treatment of impetigo caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) or Streptococcus pyogenes. For patients aged 9 months or older, a thin layer of the ointment should be applied to the affected area, covering up to 2% of the body surface area, twice daily for 5 days. For infants under 9 months, the safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established. This medication is for topical use only and should not be applied to mucosal surfaces, including the eyes, nose, mouth, or vaginal area, as its safety and efficacy in these regions have not been evaluated. If irritation or sensitization occurs, discontinue use immediately. Application site irritation has been reported in approximately 2% of cases. Epistaxis (nosebleeds) has been observed when used on nasal mucosa. There is no available data on the use of retapamulin in pregnant women to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. However, systemic absorption of the drug following topical administration is negligible, and maternal use is not expected to result in fetal exposure. Similarly, there is no data on the presence of the drug in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. Given the negligible systemic absorption, breastfeeding is not expected to expose the infant to the drug. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the medication and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant. Retapamulin is a pleuromutilin antibacterial agent that binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. It exhibits bacteriostatic activity at minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and bactericidal activity at concentrations 1000 times the MIC. The drug has low systemic absorption, is 94% protein-bound, and undergoes metabolism in vitro via the liver enzyme CYP3A4. To use this medication, clean and dry the affected area before application. Apply a small amount of ointment to the affected area as directed by your physician, typically twice daily for 5 days. You may cover the treated area with a bandage or gauze. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Improvement, such as healed or dry sores and reduced redness, should be noticeable within 3 to 4 days. Common side effects include mild burning, stinging, or itching at the application site. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to secondary infections, such as fungal infections. Serious allergic reactions are rare. If you experience severe symptoms, such as difficulty breathing or passing out, seek emergency medical attention immediately. Before using retapamulin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of retapamulin or increase the risk of side effects. Maintain a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your healthcare provider. If someone swallows this medication, it may be harmful. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center or seek emergency medical attention immediately. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
